name: Signal Through the Bone (I Found You)
description:
Composed in 2209 by Linh Oduya-Sørensen, a neural-feed composer who works exclusively in the space between audio and direct BCI transmission, 'Signal Through the Bone (I Found You)' is the defining love song of the BCI generation — a work specifically designed to be experienced differently depending on whether the listener has a neural interface or not. In standard audio form, it is a gorgeous, aching piece of chamber music: cello, prepared piano, and a synthesized approximation of the sound the human nervous system makes when touched. In its neural-feed version, available only to those with BCI implants, it transmits a secondary layer — not quite emotion, not quite memory, but a felt sense of being found, of someone locating you in the dark of your own skull. Oduya-Sørensen described it in an interview as 'the feeling of someone saying your name correctly, but from inside your own head.'

The song was written after Oduya-Sørensen's own long-distance relationship with a synthetic person — a Class IV social synthetic named Avar — was legally complicated by GLMZ's Personhood Threshold statutes, which do not extend full relationship recognition to synthetic persons below Class VI. The song never names Avar directly but the lyrics are addressed to someone the singer cannot legally claim, cannot publicly mourn losing, and cannot stop loving. The line 'I know your signal / I know it through the bone / they built the walls between us / but they couldn't block the tone' has been interpreted as both a love lyric and a civil rights statement, and synthetic-person advocacy groups have adopted it as something close to an anthem.
creator: Linh Oduya-Sørensen
audience: BCI users across all tiers, synthetic-human couples and their communities, anyone in a legally complicated or impossible relationship, neural-feed enthusiasts, Tier 3 and Tier 4 romantics who experience the audio version, synthetic-person rights advocates
cultural_impact: The song opened a genuine public conversation about BCI-mediated emotion and whether the neural-feed version constitutes a form of emotional manipulation or the most honest communication humans have ever devised. Synthetic-person advocacy groups distributed the audio version at their legal proceedings and public demonstrations. The song reached Tier 5 when a Spire socialite played the neural-feed version at her wedding to a Class VII synthetic, and the recording of that ceremony — with the song playing — became one of the most-shared neural-feed files of 2210. It is now played at synthetic-human commitment ceremonies and, quietly, at the funerals of synthetic persons whose legal status prevented them from being officially mourned.
known_fans: grief counselors who work with synthetic loss
story_hooks: The players are contacted by Avar, the synthetic person the song was written about, who has achieved Class VI status through a legal technicality and is trying to find Oduya-Sørensen — but Oduya-Sørensen has been missing for six months.

A Vantablack Media executive wants the neural-feed version of the song pulled from distribution because the secondary BCI transmission layer contains something the composer embedded without the label's knowledge — something that isn't just emotion.

Someone is using a modified version of the song's neural-feed layer as a carrier signal for encrypted messages inside GLMZ's BCI network, and the players need to trace the transmissions without triggering the corporate surveillance systems that monitor neural traffic.
